logs.title: Errors and worse, every host
logs.description: Everything logged as err, crit, alert or emerg: the first place to look when something broke.

logs.title: Warnings and worse from one host
logs.description: Replace <host> with a host from Sources, such as mikrotik. Add -word to leave out a noisy line.

logs.title: SSH logins that worked
logs.description: Every successful SSH login: who, from where and with a key or a password. A login from an address you don't know deserves a look.

logs.title: Failed SSH logins
logs.description: Wrong passwords. A steady stream from many addresses is the internet's background noise; many from one address is someone trying.

logs.title: Logins with user names that don't exist
logs.description: Guessing at accounts (admin, test, oracle, ..): scanners, not your users.

logs.title: sudo use
logs.description: Commands run as root through sudo, with the user and the command.

logs.title: Firewall blocks (ufw)
logs.needs: rsyslog on a Linux server with ufw
logs.description: Connections a Linux server's firewall refused, with source address and port.

logs.title: Out of memory
logs.description: The kernel stopping a process to free memory: a service that grew too big, or a box that needs more memory.

logs.title: Disk trouble
logs.description: Read or write errors from the kernel: a failing disk or cable. Pair with SMART warnings (smartd).

logs.title: MikroTik: logins that failed
logs.description: Wrong passwords on the router (Winbox, SSH, web). The router should not be reachable for this from outside.

logs.title: MikroTik: firewall log
logs.needs: MikroTik syslog, firewall rules with log=yes
logs.description: Lines from firewall rules that log. Add in:ether1 to see only the WAN side, or a port such as :22.

logs.title: MikroTik: DHCP leases
logs.description: Addresses the router handed out, with the device's MAC: when a new device joined your network.

logs.title: MikroTik: interface up and down
logs.description: Ports and links going up and down: a flaky cable, a device that restarts, or the WAN dropping.

logs.title: Switch ports going down
logs.description: Replace sw-* with your switches' names (* matches the rest). Frequent flapping on one port is a cable or a device.

logs.title: FRITZ!Box event log
logs.description: The FRITZ!Box's own events: the internet connection, DSL or cable sync, logins to the box, Wi-Fi.

logs.title: FRITZ!Box: internet connection changes
logs.description: When the internet connection dropped and came back, and the new address it got.

logs.title: Docker containers
logs.description: Warnings and worse that Vector sent as JSON lines, such as container logs. Narrow it with app:<container>.

logs.title: One sender, everything
logs.description: All lines of one host, newest first: turn on Live to follow it.

metrics.title: Server load
metrics.description: The 1-minute load average per server. Above the number of CPU cores, work is waiting.

metrics.title: Memory available
metrics.description: How much memory the kernel can still give out, per server. Close to zero means swapping or the out-of-memory killer.

metrics.title: Free disk space
metrics.description: Space left per mount. Alert on it before a full disk stops a database.

metrics.title: Network traffic per interface
metrics.description: Bytes per second received per network interface (a counter, so as a rate). Add a query with node_network_transmit_bytes_total for the other direction.

metrics.title: Internet throughput (FRITZ!Box)
metrics.description: Down and up on the internet line, in bytes per second. Compare with the line's maximum (fritz.max_bitrate_down/up, in bits).

metrics.title: Internet line up (FRITZ!Box)
metrics.description: 1 while the line is connected, 0 when it dropped: use No data / a metric rule below 1 to be told.

metrics.title: Router CPU (MikroTik)
metrics.description: The router's CPU, with the band of what is normal for the hour: a busy router is often a flood or a loop.

metrics.title: Router interface traffic (MikroTik)
metrics.description: Bytes per second received per router interface.

metrics.title: Exporters answering
metrics.description: 1 when a scrape target answered, 0 when it didn't, per target: a server or exporter that is down.

metrics.title: Vigil itself
metrics.description: Records waiting to be written, and records dropped per second. A growing queue means the database is slow or away.
